Those things are as close to fact as is reasonable. If you put energy into a system, you get heat. Greenhouse gases can be observed trapping heat. These are trivial to reproduce and you can even do them in your own home.

Turn on a light. Touch it. It is warmer. Use baking soda and vinegar, trap the gases in a glass bottle, and put two of the same glass jugs into the window. Now measure the temperature differences after an hour.

Those are as close to fact as we get in science. There is no (realistic) doubt that we are increasing the speed the planet is warming at.

Where doubt arrives is when we ask how much, how rapidly, and what the results are going to be. Those are NOT "settled" science, regardless of what the doom-sayers tell the public.

You kick out (or change) the outliers, because you're looking for accuracy with your predictions. That's perfectly normal.

So, again, the climate is changing. Our output of greenhouse gases is affecting the rate that the climate is changing. Our activities are, beyond reasonable doubt, causing the global temperature to rise as an average. There are still questions, but those are as close to factual as science gets.
